checks: The inverse divides by the positive scale s, so the homogeneous cap identity holds for any positive L. The perspective cone over C is convex by reweighting inverse points with their positive scales. A positive affine L imposes exactly the single affine slice equation.

At fixed label z, Z=zs and ell(z)s+c·Y=1 give the d-plane. When c is nonzero its direction space has a vector with delta s=1, which cannot be in the direction space at a distinct label. On a full-dimensional old fiber L varies, hence Z varies when z is nonzero.

After rotating c, the d−1 transverse derivative columns are L^(−1) times coordinate unit vectors. The orthogonal component of the remaining column is L^(−2) times the vector with entries ell in the c-direction and −(z,1)|c| in the base and scale directions. This proves the displayed positive Jacobian. The c=0 direct dilation matches, and an exact two-coordinate Gram calculation also checked ell=0.
Injectivity and area change give the density by dividing the original 1/L by the Jacobian. No sign restriction on ell is needed because s is retained.

For a finite affine minimum the cone inequalities are A_j^hom≥1 and the graph has equality in at least one. Fixing an active j makes that locus a convex slice. In the square example the lifted midpoint has minimum homogeneous value 2. The dropped-scale midpoint has no inverse in the square, and strictly increasing radius along each ray proves injectivity.
Source bd4e19d78aaec9e1 §§5–6, (13)–(17), contains the square example, equations, and Gram argument. The frozen proof derives the identities directly.

overlap.comparison: Its proof records the original base-label equation in homogeneous coordinates and a full ambient projective determinant. It does not compute the intrinsic d-Jacobian with a retained scale or the finite-minimum locus and nonconvexity.

It gives full projective orbit hull and cap preservation for base-only denominators after dropping scale. This draft also treats continuous denominators, nonparallel old fiber planes, and piecewise-affine minima.

readability: The derivative proof factors L^(−1) from each column before taking the remaining orthogonal component. The first component of that factored column is ell/L.

summary: The homogeneous affine and finite-minimum descriptions are exact. The intrinsic Jacobian follows from the Gram volume calculation, including a zero constant term on a positive fiber.
